parts.text: Which claim correctly explains why the bottle crumples?

options.text: Outside atmospheric pressure is greater than the pressure inside the bottle, so outside air pushes the walls in.
Air pressure inside the bottle is greater than outside, so the walls are pushed out and then snap back.
The bottle crumples even when the air pressure outside equals the air pressure inside.
Atmospheric air around the bottle pulls the walls inward with no pressure difference needed.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Leela pumps most of the air out of a thin plastic bottle and seals it. The bottle crumples inward.

part_answers.answer: Removing air lowers pressure inside; higher outside atmospheric pressure then pushes the bottle walls inward.

teacher.key_rationale: A pressure difference is needed: higher outside atmospheric pressure pushes the walls in when inside pressure is lowered.
